symptom: Project rules told AI agents to fix root causes, but a high-risk change could still satisfy the contract gate with non-empty prose that did not identify a real shared boundary, same-class entries, class-level tests, obsolete paths, or a dependency upgrade decision.
direct_cause: P2 and R21 repeated guidance across always-loaded text while schema v1 validated mostly field presence and the local reminder hook was gitignored, so execution quality depended on each agent remembering and interpreting the rule.
class_root: The repository expressed root-cause remediation as advisory prose instead of a versioned evidence contract whose claims are cross-checked against real paths, changed tests, immutable history, and CI.
affected_population: Users whose defects are handled by Claude, Codex, Cursor, or another repository-aware coding agent
Maintainers reviewing high-risk provider, media, workflow, task, runtime, IPC, persistence, and compatibility repairs
entry_points: Claude reads CLAUDE.md and the triggered root-cause-remediation skill before corrective production work
Codex and other AGENTS-aware tools read generated AGENTS.md and the same repository skill
Local and GitHub validation run check:root-cause-contracts before merge
internal_only_reason: This defect concerns Nomi's own repository instruction and CI contract. The enforcement invariant is decided by committed project files; external agent documentation cannot prove whether this repository's evidence paths and tests match its changes.
invariants: P2 and R21 remain the only always-loaded root-cause rule identifiers; detailed procedure lives once in the repository skill.
AGENTS.md is generated from CLAUDE.md, so Claude and Codex cannot drift into separately maintained remediation rules.

Every new or modified contract uses schema v3 and identifies recurrence, real shared boundaries, at least two checked same-class entries, structural prevention, changed class tests, legacy-path disposition, and dependency lifecycle.

Historical schema v1 and v2 contracts remain readable only while their byte content matches either the committed bootstrap hash baseline or the trusted target-base snapshot; editing or adding a legacy contract relative to that base fails CI.
The committed contract gate, not a machine-local hook, is the merge authority.
generality_proof: The trigger is phrased by corrective intent rather than one product directory, and the same skill is referenced from both generated agent instruction surfaces. For mechanically high-risk paths, one checker validates every changed contract and covered file regardless of which agent, provider, platform, or defect produced the diff.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Reject unproven schema-v3 remediation evidence and any legacy history that is new, deleted, or modified relative to the trusted target base before a high-risk change can pass contracts.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Claude receives the short trigger and is directed to the single detailed skill before production edits.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: generated P2 and R21 corrective-change trigger
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Codex receives the same trigger because AGENTS.md is regenerated and checked against CLAUDE.md.
The checker hashes every contract, inherits immutable v1 history from ROOT_CAUSE_BASE_REF, and runs the v2 cross-field validator on the repository diff.
The merge workflow invokes the committed contracts command, and its structure test prevents the gate from being silently removed or reordered out of the validation path.

recurrence.reason: Every concurrent agent or PR can otherwise invent a locally complete but incompatible remediation schema, so the collision can recur whenever governance evolves in parallel.
same_class_scan: Compared every root-cause contract schema, template, skill instruction, always-loaded rule, checker, and CI entry point from PR #221 and the latest main branch.
Verified schema v1, both incompatible schema v2 shapes, new schema v3 contracts, changed legacy contracts, and target-base-only legacy history.

prevention.invariant: A high-risk corrective diff cannot pass using a patch-shaped, pathless, testless, or lifecycle-free root-cause narrative.
prevention.failure_mode: The contracts command exits nonzero with the missing or inconsistent evidence before unit, package, or merge validation can report success.
prevention.strategy: Give the merged recurrence and shared-boundary contract one new schema version, preserve earlier versions as immutable target-base history, and make CI reject any new or edited legacy shape.

legacy_paths.rationale: The schema-v1 path that accepted mutable non-empty prose is replaced by v2 validation plus a content-hash-only historical reader; no path can create or edit v1 successfully.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The checker uses Node built-ins and repository JSON; no third-party runtime or package version controls this enforcement contract.

migration: Existing schema-v1 hashes bootstrap from scripts/root-cause-contract-v1-baseline.json; every schema-v1 or schema-v2 contract on the trusted ROOT_CAUSE_BASE_REF is inherited by exact SHA-256. They remain readable as immutable incident history. Any edit or PR-local legacy addition must migrate to schema v3.
residual_risks: No static checker can prove an agent's private reasoning or detect a deliberately false statement. The gate instead makes evidence falsifiable by tying claims to repository paths and changed tests.

Low-risk corrective paths are governed by the mandatory P2/skill trigger but are not all mechanically classified; expanding mechanical coverage should follow observed misses rather than forcing root-cause contracts onto unrelated feature work.
